summary.title: Programming Projects for Advanced Beginners #3a: Tic-Tac-Toe AI
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a command-line Tic-Tac-Toe engine by breaking a large project into small milestones (board, render, input, moves, win and draw checks), with the aim of later building an unbeatable AI.
keywords: build tic tac toe in python
takeaways: Break a big program into a skeleton of small, isolated functions such as new_board, render, get_move, make_move, get_winner and is_board_full.
Represent the 3x3 board as a list of lists and write make_move so it returns a new board rather than mutating its input.
Make illegal moves raise an exception, and keep move validation in a separate function such as is_valid_move.
Check for a winner by building all rows, columns and diagonals and testing each for three identical marks; check for a draw when the board is full.
Run code after every small milestone so bugs are easy to find.
summary.summary: This is part 3a of a project series for advanced beginners, in which the author guides the reader through building a command-line Tic-Tac-Toe game for two human players. The article uses a pseudocode skeleton to split the work into milestones: creating the board, rendering it, getting input, executing moves, detecting winners and draws. It emphasises design choices such as immutability, error handling for illegal moves, and frequent testing. The engine built here is the foundation for part 3b, where the human players are replaced with AI players.
